transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because... I've just been really, really driven lately. Which is usually a good thing, right? Especially in IT management. I just can't seem to stop launching new projects. I've been drawing up all these new work plans, setting up aggressive certification schedules, doing massive home network upgrades... even messaging a bunch of old contacts. 

I honestly thought I was just being super productive, but... well, I guess I can see how it gets a little intense. I kind of blow past normal limits, and I don't really notice until my wife or my director has to step in and tell me to slow down. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this the right way.
During these times, have you ever heard or seen things that other people could not?

Um... wow, well. I really want to be completely open with you, Doctor, but I hope this doesn't make me sound... you know, bad. 

I wouldn't say I'm hearing voices or anything scary like that. It's just... sometimes, when I'm working late and nobody else is there? Like if I'm alone in my home office, or if I'm near the server room and there's that constant, heavy hum from the cooling fans... I'll think I hear my name. 

Or sometimes it's just these really short, quick comments. Like someone saying, "check the logs," or... or "they know." 

But I always just assumed it was the white noise, you know? Just my brain trying to make words out of the hum because I've been pushing myself so hard with all the network upgrades. That's probably pretty normal when you're overtired, right? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Have you ever had any fixed beliefs during these periods that other people said weren’t true?

Um... gosh, I really want to give you the right answer here, but I'm a little embarrassed to admit this part. I don't want you to think I'm... you know, paranoid or anything. But... yeah, sometimes I do get these ideas. 

And it's actually not just when I'm in one of those really intense, driven phases. Even when my mood is totally normal and I'm not having a big swing, I'll start noticing things at work. Like, um, certain calendar invites that don't include me, or the exact timing of someone changing their Teams status, or just passing comments in the hallway... and I get completely convinced that they are coded warnings. Like everyone is secretly building a case to push me out of the company. 

People tell me it's not true. My wife says I'm just reading way too much into things, and my director says my job is totally safe. And I know office politics can make anyone a little hyper-vigilant, right? I'm sure it's just normal corporate stress getting out of hand. 

I try really hard to keep it to myself so I don't bother anyone with it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I really hope I'm giving you the information you need.
Have you ever had a period like this before when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable, with much more energy than usual?

Um... well, yes, I suppose I have. I mean, I really hope this doesn't make me sound difficult to be around, because I always try to be a good husband and a good manager. But... yeah, there are times when it feels like that. 

Some weeks I just feel... almost electric, you know? Like I'm completely unstoppable and I can tackle any problem the network throws at me. It feels great, honestly. But... and I feel terrible admitting this... sometimes during those weeks, if there's even a tiny delay, or if my wife just asks a simple question about what I'm doing... I can kind of snap. 

It's not that I want to be mean! It's just... in that moment, it feels like everyone is deliberately trying to slow me down on purpose, and I get so irritable. I always feel awful about it afterward, because I know they're just trying to help. I really try to keep a lid on it, I promise. 

Is that normal for someone who's just really passionate about their work? I hope I'm not sounding too... unstable or anything.
How long has your most intense recent period of unusually high energy or irritability lasted continuously?

Um... gosh, let me think. I really want to be accurate for you. 

If we're talking about those stretches where I'm just... you know, super driven, not needing much sleep, and feeling like I can take on the whole world... I guess those have been happening for a while now. 

I'd say... maybe roughly a year and eight months? Give or take? 

I know that sounds like a long time to be dealing with this kind of thing, and I really hope you don't think I've just been ignoring a problem. I always just thought I was going through phases of being really dedicated to my job, you know? Like I was just being a really good, productive employee. 

I really try my best to handle it well. Does... does that timeframe make sense to you? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of timeline.
During your most intense recent period, did you ever need to be hospitalized or become unable to function safely at work or at home?

Um... well, no, I haven't been hospitalized. I really try to keep things manageable, you know? I don't want to be a burden on anyone. But... I guess things did get a little out of hand recently. 

I'm actually... well, I'm on a leave of absence from work right now. There was this big network migration, and I was so sure I had the perfect plan, but... it failed. And I guess my reaction to it wasn't... ideal. They suggested I take some time off. I really hope they don't think I'm a bad manager, I was just so invested in it working.

And at home... my wife is wonderful, she really is. She's just had to... step in a bit more lately. Like, she's keeping an eye on our spending because I bought some servers I didn't really need, and she has to remind me to stop working at 3 AM. And... sometimes our conversations turn into arguments if she interrupts me when I'm really focused. I feel terrible about it, I really do. I don't mean to be difficult.

I've even had to step back from some things I love, like playing music at church, rock climbing, and this mentoring program I was doing. I just... I can't seem to reliably show up or follow through right now, and I hate letting people down. 

Is that... does that answer your question? I know it sounds like a lot, but I'm really trying to get back on track. I hope I'm not coming across as too much of a mess.
During your most intense periods, have you ever needed very little sleep and still felt full of energy the next day?

Um... well, yes, I suppose that happens sometimes. I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm neglecting my health on purpose, because I do know how important sleep is. I really try to take care of myself.

But... yeah, there have been these runs where I'll sleep maybe... three hours? And I'll wake up sharp at 3 or 4 a.m. But the strange thing is, I don't feel exhausted or anything. I actually feel like I've been handed this... this bonus time, you know? Like I've got a head start on the day to get things done. I feel totally fine, honestly. 

I just... I use that time to be productive. Is that... is it okay that I feel that way? I just figure if my body is awake and ready to go, I should make the most of it, right? I hope that makes sense.
Have you ever needed to be hospitalized because of these symptoms?

Oh, um... I know I touched on this just a little bit ago, but... no, I've never been hospitalized for any of this. I'm so sorry if I wasn't clear enough the first time, I really hope I didn't confuse you. 

I really do try my absolute best to keep things manageable so it never gets to that point. I just... I wouldn't want to be a burden on the medical staff or take up a bed when someone else might need it much more than I do, you know? So, no, no hospitals. 

Did... did I say something earlier that made it sound like I should have been? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the exact right information.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest or pleasure in things?

Um... well, I really try to stay positive, you know? I think having a good attitude is so important. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, there have been some stretches... maybe a couple weeks at a time... where it's a bit harder. 

I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I have a great life, but... sometimes I'll wake up and just feel like... like a failed version of myself. It's this heavy, flat feeling. And I feel so guilty about it, because my wife will just ask me normal questions, like what I want for dinner, and it just feels like... like too much effort to even answer. I really hate being that way with her, she doesn't deserve it. 

I try to snap out of it as quickly as I can, though. I don't want to bring anyone else down. Is... is it normal to feel that way sometimes? I hope I don't sound too negative.
Have you ever had a separate period that lasted at least a week where your mood was clearly elevated or irritable and your energy was much higher than usual?

Um... well, I really hope this doesn't make me sound like a difficult person, because I truly try to be easygoing. But... yes, there are definitely times, usually lasting a week or more, where I just feel... I don't know, almost electric? Like I'm completely unstoppable and my energy is just through the roof. 

It's actually a great feeling, very productive, like I mentioned before. But... and I feel terrible admitting this... sometimes during those weeks, I can get a little... irritable? Like, if there's a tiny delay in something, or if my wife asks me a simple question, I might snap at her. It's awful, I know. It just feels in those moments like everyone is deliberately trying to slow me down on purpose, and I get so frustrated. 

I always apologize right away, of course. I really don't want you to think I'm a mean husband or anything like that. I love my wife very much. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you ever felt completely convinced that people were trying to control, harm, or monitor you in a way that others said was not real?

Um... gosh, that's a tough one to talk about. I really don't want to sound paranoid or... or like I'm making a big deal out of nothing. I know I'm probably just overthinking things sometimes, you know? 

But... well, yes, sometimes I do get these... these really strong feelings. And it's strange because it happens even when my mood is totally fine, like when I'm not feeling super down or super energized. I just... I get completely convinced that things happening at work are actually aimed at me. 

Like... um... if I see certain calendar invites pop up, or if someone changes their Teams status, or even just passing comments in the hallway... I get this overwhelming feeling that they're actually coded warnings. Like everyone is secretly building a case to push me out of my job. 

My wife tells me I'm just reading too much into things, and maybe I am. I really try not to let it affect how I treat my coworkers, because I want to be a good manager and a team player. I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything. Is it... is it common to get a little overly suspicious like that sometimes?
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when you felt unusually elevated or irritable and had much more energy than usual, even when you were not depressed?

Um... well, I know we just talked a bit about those times when my energy gets really high, and... I hope I'm understanding your question right, but yes, those elevated periods definitely happen even when I'm not feeling down at all. 

Actually, if I'm being totally honest—and I really don't want it to sound like I'm totally out of control or anything, because I really do try my best to manage everything at work and at home—but... looking back over the last couple of years, those high-energy, sort of pressured phases... they've actually taken up a lot more time than the stretches where I feel flat, or even just the normal, quiet times in between. 

It's just... I'm always trying to be productive and do a good job, you know? But I guess those really intense, elevated weeks have become the most common thing for me lately. I hope that's okay to admit. Does that make sense for what you're asking?

Have you ever had a period when your mood and energy were so high that you became so impaired that others had to stop you, or you did things that caused major problems at work, at home, or with the law?

Um... gosh, I really hate admitting this, because I pride myself on being a good provider and a hard worker. I really hope you don't judge me too harshly for it... but, yes, there have been some problems. I always try my best to do the right thing, but... well, recently at work, I was pushing really hard on this big system migration, working all hours because I felt so energized, and... well, it failed. They actually had to put me on leave for a bit. I felt just terrible about letting my company down.

And at home... my wife, she's so incredibly patient with me, but she's had to step in and kind of take the reins sometimes. Mostly just to help manage things, like stepping in around my spending when I get a little too overenthusiastic, or trying to pull me away from all that late-night work. And like I mentioned before, sometimes our conversations turn into arguments because I'm just moving too fast and get frustrated. I hate putting that burden on her. 

I've actually pulled away from some of the things I usually love doing, too... like playing music at church, going rock climbing, and the mentoring program I'm part of. I just... I realized I can't reliably show up or follow through on my commitments right now, and I'd rather step back than disappoint people. I really am trying my hardest to get back on track and fix all of this, though. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you ever had times when the suspicious thoughts or hearing your name happened even when you were not having any mood episode at all?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I really don't want to make it sound like I'm completely out of touch with reality all the time, because I'm really not. I try so hard to stay grounded. But... well, yes. 

There have been these... these stretches where I feel totally fine. Just calm, you know? Not overly energized, not down at all. Sometimes for a few weeks at a time. I'll just be feeling normal, but... I'll still get that strong feeling that the Teams statuses are those coded warnings. And... um... I'll still hear those little comments or my name being called when no one is actually there. 

It's really embarrassing to admit that, honestly. I try to just ignore it and keep working hard, so I don't bother anyone with it. I hope that doesn't make me sound too strange. Is it... is it helpful that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest or pleasure in things?

Um... well, yes, I suppose I have. I mean, I try really hard not to let it get to me, and I know everyone has their off days, right? I really try to push through it and stay positive for my wife, because she does so much for me. But... yeah, there have been some times, definitely longer than a couple of weeks, where I just... I don't know. 

There are these stretches where I'll wake up and just feel like... like a failed version of myself, if that makes sense? It's just this heavy, flat feeling. And I hate it, because I want to be a good husband and a good worker, but during those times, even just answering my wife's normal, everyday questions feels like it takes more energy than I have. It just feels like too much. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or ungrateful for the life I have. I know I have a lot to be thankful for. I just... sometimes that heavy feeling really sticks around. Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Have you ever had at least two weeks when you had those hallucinations or suspicious beliefs but did not have any major mood symptoms like feeling unusually energized, irritable, or depressed?

Um... yes, I think we touched on this a little bit earlier, but... yes. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. 

But, yes, there have definitely been stretches—several times, actually, for a few weeks at a time—where my mood was just... fine. I wasn't feeling that intense, buzzing energy, and I wasn't feeling that heavy, flat depression either. I was just kind of... calm. Normal, really. But even during those calm weeks, I... well, I still had those strong beliefs that the Teams statuses were those coded warnings about me. And I'd still hear those little comments, or my name, when the room was completely empty. 

I really try to just push past it when it happens, because I don't want to make a big deal out of nothing or worry my wife when I'm otherwise doing okay. It's just... it's hard to admit that my mind plays tricks on me even when my mood is completely stable. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be as helpful as possible for you.
Have you ever had a time when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks while your hallucinations or suspicious beliefs were still happening?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try to keep things separate in my head, you know? Like, if I'm feeling that heavy, down feeling... usually, those Teams messages and the voices kind of fade into the background. It's almost like I don't have the energy to even notice them when I'm feeling that low. 

I hope I'm remembering that right. I really try not to dwell on the bad times too much, so sometimes the details get a little fuzzy. But... yeah, I'm pretty sure that when I'm feeling really down for a couple of weeks, those other things aren't really happening at the same time. Does that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you accurate information.
Have these suspicious beliefs and hearing your name been going on continuously for at least two years?

Um... no, not quite two years. I mean, I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm making a big deal out of something that hasn't even been going on that long. I know some people deal with things for their whole lives, and I really admire how strong they are. 

For me, it's been... maybe about a year and a half? Give or take? That's when I first started noticing the, um, the coded messages on Teams and hearing those little comments. I've really tried my best to manage it on my own since then, you know, just keeping my head down and doing my work. I hope a year and a half doesn't sound like I've just been letting it get out of hand... I really have been trying to stay on top of it. Does that timeline help you? I can try to pinpoint the exact month if you need me to, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were feeling completely normal—neither depressed nor unusually energized—but the suspicious beliefs or hearing your name were still happening?

Um, yes, actually. I think we might have touched on this just a little bit earlier, but... yes. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I know your time is valuable and I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. 

But, yes, there have definitely been stretches—a few times, for maybe a few weeks at a time—where my mood was just... fine. Calm, or maybe a little flat. I wasn't feeling that intense, buzzing energy, and I wasn't feeling heavy or depressed either. I was just kind of... normal, really. But even during those calm weeks, I... well, I still had those strong beliefs that the Teams statuses were those coded warnings about me. And I'd still hear those little comments, or my name, when the room was completely empty. 

I really try to just push past it when it happens, because I don't want to make a big deal out of nothing or worry anyone when I'm otherwise doing okay. It's just... it's a little embarrassing to admit that my mind plays tricks on me even when my mood is completely stable. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be as helpful as possible for you. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing or believing these things while your mood was completely normal?

Um, yes... I think you might have just asked me that, actually. I'm sorry, I hope I'm not being confusing or... or talking in circles. I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. 

But yes, like I was saying, there have definitely been a few times—maybe a couple of weeks at a stretch—where my mood was just... completely fine. You know, calm, or maybe a little flat. I wasn't feeling super energized, and I wasn't feeling down at all. Just a normal, even mood. 

But even then, during those totally calm weeks, I... I still had that strong feeling that the Teams statuses were those coded warnings. And I'd still hear those little comments when no one was around. I try so hard to just ignore it when it happens so I don't bother anyone, but... yeah, it still happens even when my mood is totally normal. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. Did I explain that okay?
